questions.text: 'विश्व मानव विकास सूचकांक' से संबंधित निम्नलिखित तालिका का अध्ययन कीजिए और उसके नीचे दिए गए प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए: क्र. सं. | देश | विश्व में मानव विकास सूचकांक का क्रमांक 1. भारत - 130, 2. म्यांमार - 148, 3. नेपाल - 149, 4. पाकिस्तान - 150. दिए गए देशों में से, निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा देश 'मानव विकास सूचकांक' में उच्चतम स्थान रखता है?
questions.text_english: Study the following table related to 'World Human Development Index' and answer the question given below: S.No. | Country | HDI Rank in the world: 1. India - 130, 2. Myanmar - 148, 3. Nepal - 149, 4. Pakistan - 150. Amongst the given countries, which one of the following countries has the highest rank in 'Human Development Index'?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) India. In the Human Development Index, a lower rank number indicates a higher (better) position. Among the given countries, India has rank 130, which is the lowest number and therefore the highest position. Myanmar (148), Nepal (149), and Pakistan (150) all have higher rank numbers, meaning they are placed lower than India on the HDI.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) भारत है। मानव विकास सूचकांक में कम क्रमांक का अर्थ उच्च स्थान होता है। दिए गए देशों में भारत का क्रमांक 130 है, जो सबसे कम संख्या है और इसलिए सर्वोच्च स्थान है। म्यांमार (148), नेपाल (149) और पाकिस्तान (150) का क्रमांक अधिक है, अर्थात वे भारत से नीचे हैं।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से राजनीतिक दल के मुख्य घटक हैं? सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए: I. नेता, II. सक्रिय सदस्य, III. समर्थक, IV. दबाव समूह
questions.text_english: Which of the following are the main components of a political party? Choose the correct option: I. Leaders, II. Active members, III. Followers, IV. Pressure groups

options.A: केवल I, II और III सही हैं।
options.B: केवल II, III और IV सही हैं।
options.C: केवल I, III और IV सही हैं।
options.D: केवल I, II और IV सही हैं।

options_english.A: Only I, II and III are correct.
options_english.B: Only II, III and IV are correct.
options_english.C: Only I, III and IV are correct.
options_english.D: Only I, II and IV are correct.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Only I, II and III are correct. The three main components of a political party are its Leaders (who make decisions and represent the party), Active Members (who work for the party at the ground level), and Followers (who support and vote for the party). Pressure groups (IV) are not components of a political party; they are separate organisations that try to influence government policy from outside.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) केवल I, II और III सही हैं। राजनीतिक दल के तीन मुख्य घटक हैं — नेता, सक्रिय सदस्य और समर्थक। दबाव समूह राजनीतिक दल का हिस्सा नहीं होते; वे बाहर से सरकारी नीतियों को प्रभावित करने का प्रयास करते हैं।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से सही सुमेलित युग्म का चयन कीजिए: (देश) — (व्यवस्था): (A) कनाडा — एकात्मक, (B) बोलीविया — संघात्मक, (C) ऑस्ट्रेलिया — एकात्मक, (D) स्पेन — संघात्मक
questions.text_english: Choose the correctly matched pair from the following: (Country) — (System): (A) Canada — Unitary, (B) Bolivia — Federal, (C) Australia — Unitary, (D) Spain — Federal
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Spain — Federal. Spain has a federal system of government with significant powers devolved to its autonomous communities. Canada has a federal system (not unitary), so option A is wrong. Bolivia also has a unitary system (not federal), so option B is wrong. Australia follows a federal system (not unitary), so option C is wrong. Therefore, Spain — Federal is the only correctly matched pair.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) स्पेन — संघात्मक है। स्पेन में संघात्मक शासन प्रणाली है। कनाडा संघात्मक है (एकात्मक नहीं), बोलीविया एकात्मक है (संघात्मक नहीं), और ऑस्ट्रेलिया संघात्मक है (एकात्मक नहीं)।

questions.text: बेल्जियम ने अपनी बहुसंख्यकवाद की समस्या का समाधान निम्नलिखित में से किस प्रकार की शासन व्यवस्था को सुदृढ़ करके किया?
questions.text_english: Belgium solved its problem of majoritarianism by strengthening which of the following types of government?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Federal. Belgium faced the problem of majoritarianism because the Dutch-speaking majority dominated the French-speaking minority. To resolve this, Belgium strengthened its federal system by dividing power between the central government and regional governments (Flanders, Wallonia, and Brussels). This ensured that no single linguistic community could dominate the others, making power-sharing constitutionally guaranteed.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) संघात्मक है। बेल्जियम में डच-भाषी बहुसंख्यकों और फ्रांसीसी-भाषी अल्पसंख्यकों के बीच टकराव था। इसे सुलझाने के लिए बेल्जियम ने संघात्मक व्यवस्था को मजबूत किया और सत्ता को केंद्र व क्षेत्रीय सरकारों में बाँटा।

questions.text: स्तंभ I का स्तंभ II से मिलान कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए: स्तंभ I (खनिज) — स्तंभ II (प्रमुख खानें): a. लौह अयस्क — i. गया, b. अभ्रक — ii. सिंगरौली, c. बॉक्साइट — iii. चंद्रपुर, d. कोयला — iv. मैकाल
questions.text_english: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option: Column I (Minerals) — Column II (Major Mines): a. Iron ore — i. Gaya, b. Mica — ii. Singarauli, c. Bauxite — iii. Chandrapur, d. Coal — iv. Maikala
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii. Iron ore (a) is found in Chandrapur (iii) in Maharashtra. Mica (b) is predominantly found in Gaya (i) in Bihar. Bauxite (c) has significant deposits in the Maikala (iv) hills range. Coal (d) is found in Singarauli (ii) in Madhya Pradesh/UP region. Therefore, the correct matching is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii है। लौह अयस्क — चंद्रपुर, अभ्रक — गया, बॉक्साइट — मैकाल, कोयला — सिंगरौली।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा क्षेत्र 1866 में एकीकृत इटली का हिस्सा बना?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following regions became a part of unified Italy in 1866?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Venetia. During the unification of Italy, different regions were added at different times. Sardinia-Piedmont was the base of unification under Cavour. Sicily and the southern regions were united through Garibaldi's campaign in 1860. Venetia (Venice) joined the unified Italy in 1866 after the Austro-Prussian War, when Austria ceded it to Italy. The Papal State was incorporated last in 1870.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) वेनेशिया है। इटली के एकीकरण के दौरान विभिन्न क्षेत्र अलग-अलग समय पर जुड़े। वेनेशिया 1866 में ऑस्ट्रो-प्रशिया युद्ध के बाद एकीकृत इटली में शामिल हुआ।

questions.text: उन्नीसवीं सदी तक लोगों के यूरोप से अमेरिका जाने के निम्नलिखित कारणों को पढ़िए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए: I. ग़रीबी और भूख, II. गुलामों की खरीद-फ़रोख्त, III. बीमारियों का बोलबाला, IV. धार्मिक टकराव और दंड
questions.text_english: Read the following reasons of migration of people from Europe to America till the 19th century and choose the correct option: I. Poverty and hunger, II. Slaves for sale, III. Wide spread of diseases, IV. Religious conflicts and persecution

options.A: केवल I, II और III सही हैं।
options.B: केवल II, III और IV सही हैं।
options.C: केवल I, III और IV सही हैं।
options.D: केवल I, II और IV सही हैं।

options_english.A: Only I, II and III are correct.
options_english.B: Only II, III and IV are correct.
options_english.C: Only I, III and IV are correct.
options_english.D: Only I, II and IV are correct.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Only I, III and IV are correct. Europeans migrated to America primarily due to poverty and hunger (I), widespread diseases in Europe (III), and religious persecution and conflicts (IV). Slaves for sale (II) refers to the forced transportation of African people to America, which was not a reason for European migration but rather the slave trade. Therefore, statement II is not a reason for European migration to America.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) केवल I, III और IV सही हैं। यूरोपीय लोग गरीबी, बीमारियों और धार्मिक उत्पीड़न के कारण अमेरिका गए। गुलामों की खरीद-फ़रोख्त यूरोपीय प्रवास का कारण नहीं थी, यह अफ्रीकी दास व्यापार से संबंधित था।

questions.text: 'बुक ऑफ़ मार्वेल्स' के लेखक हैं:
questions.text_english: The author of 'Book of Marvels' is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Marco Polo. The 'Book of Marvels' (also known as 'The Travels of Marco Polo') was written by Marco Polo, the Venetian explorer who travelled to China and Central Asia in the 13th century. His accounts described the wealth and splendour of Asia and inspired later European explorers like Columbus. Columbus, Vasco da Gama, and Alfred Crosby are associated with different explorations and writings.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) मार्को पोलो है। 'बुक ऑफ़ मार्वेल्स' की रचना मार्को पोलो ने की थी, जो एक वेनिस के यात्री थे। उन्होंने 13वीं सदी में चीन और मध्य एशिया की यात्रा की और अपने अनुभव इस पुस्तक में लिखे।

questions.text: मान लीजिए कि आप 15वीं शताब्दी की प्रिंट संस्कृति पर शोध कर रहे हैं। निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा आपके शोध का सबसे महत्वपूर्ण लाभ होगा?
questions.text_english: Assume you are doing research on 15th century print culture. Which of the following would be the most significant advantage for your research?

options.C: पाठों को हाथ से कॉपी करने की क्षमता में बढ़ोतरी
options.D: प्रिंट में तेज़ी और सटीकता में वृद्धि

options_english.C: Increase in the ability to copy text by hand
options_english.D: Increased speed and accuracy of print

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Easier access to rare manuscripts. For a researcher studying 15th century print culture, the most significant advantage would be easier access to rare manuscripts, as this period marks the early development of the printing press. Access to original manuscripts from that era would provide primary evidence about what was being printed, how texts were reproduced, and how knowledge was disseminated. Options B, C, and D are not directly advantageous for historical research on early print culture.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) दुर्लभ पांडुलिपियों तक आसान पहुँच है। 15वीं शताब्दी की प्रिंट संस्कृति पर शोध के लिए दुर्लभ पांडुलिपियों तक पहुँच सबसे महत्वपूर्ण लाभ होगी, क्योंकि ये उस युग के प्राथमिक स्रोत हैं।

questions.text: भारत में वनों के निम्नलिखित वर्गों को क्षेत्रफल की दृष्टि से सबसे अधिक से सबसे कम के क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए: I. आरक्षित, II. रक्षित, III. अवर्गीकृत
questions.text_english: Arrange the following categories of forests in India from the largest to the smallest in terms of area and choose the correct option: I. Reserved, II. Protected, III. Unclassed
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) I, II, III. In India, Reserved Forests (I) cover the largest area (about 54% of total forest area) and are under strict government control with no rights granted to local people. Protected Forests (II) cover a moderate area (about 29%), where some rights may be given. Unclassed Forests (III) cover the smallest area (about 17%) and are owned by government, private individuals, or communities.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) I, II, III है। भारत में आरक्षित वन सर्वाधिक (लगभग 54%) क्षेत्रफल में फैले हैं, उसके बाद रक्षित वन (लगभग 29%), और सबसे कम अवर्गीकृत वन (लगभग 17%) हैं।

questions.text: 'सरिस्का बाघ रिज़र्व' निम्नलिखित में से किस राज्य में स्थित है?
questions.text_english: 'Sariska Tiger Reserve' is located in which one of the following states?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Rajasthan. Sariska Tiger Reserve is located in the Alwar district of Rajasthan. It is one of India's prominent tiger reserves established under Project Tiger. It is situated in the Aravalli mountain range. Madhya Pradesh is known for Kanha, Bandhavgarh, and Pench Tiger Reserves. Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and Maharashtra do not have the Sariska reserve.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) राजस्थान है। सरिस्का बाघ रिज़र्व राजस्थान के अलवर जिले में अरावली पर्वत श्रृंखला में स्थित है। यह प्रोजेक्ट टाइगर के तहत स्थापित एक प्रमुख बाघ अभयारण्य है।

questions.text: स्तंभ I का स्तंभ II से मिलान कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए: स्तंभ I (बाँध) — स्तंभ II (नदी): a. हीराकुड — i. चम्बल, b. गाँधी सागर — ii. कृष्णा, c. नागार्जुन सागर — iii. कावेरी, d. मेट्रू — iv. महानदी
questions.text_english: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option: Column I (Dam) — Column II (River): a. Hirakud — i. Chambal, b. Gandhi Sagar — ii. Krishna, c. Nagarjuna Sagar — iii. Kaveri, d. Mettur — iv. Mahanadi
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii. Hirakud Dam (a) is built on the Mahanadi river (iv) in Odisha. Gandhi Sagar Dam (b) is built on the Chambal river (i) in Madhya Pradesh. Nagarjuna Sagar Dam (c) is built on the Krishna river (ii) in Andhra Pradesh/Telangana. Mettur Dam (d) is built on the Kaveri river (iii) in Tamil Nadu.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii है। हीराकुड बाँध — महानदी, गाँधी सागर — चम्बल, नागार्जुन सागर — कृष्णा, मेट्टूर — कावेरी।

questions.text: कृष्णा – गोदावरी मुद्दे में शामिल प्रमुख राज्यों से संबंधित सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:
questions.text_english: Choose the correct option regarding major states involved in the Krishna – Godavari issue:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. The Krishna-Godavari river water dispute is a long-standing inter-state conflict primarily involving Maharashtra (where both rivers originate), Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh (through which they flow and drain into the Bay of Bengal). These states dispute water-sharing rights for irrigation and drinking purposes. Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Odisha are not primarily involved in this particular dispute.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) महाराष्ट्र, कर्नाटक और आँध्र प्रदेश है। कृष्णा-गोदावरी नदी जल विवाद मुख्य रूप से इन्हीं तीन राज्यों के बीच है, जो इन नदियों के उद्गम और प्रवाह क्षेत्र से जुड़े हैं।

questions.text: कल्पना कीजिए कि आप जनवरी में दिल्ली से चंडीगढ़ एक शादी में शामिल होने के लिए, सड़क मार्ग से जा रहे हैं। यात्रा के दौरान आप निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी फ़सल खेतों में प्रमुखता से देखेंगे?
questions.text_english: Imagine you are travelling from Delhi to Chandigarh to attend a wedding, by road in January. Which of the following crops will you notice prominently in the fields during the journey?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Wheat. January falls in the Rabi (winter) crop season. The Delhi to Chandigarh route passes through Haryana and Punjab, which are the major wheat-producing states of India. Wheat is sown in October-November and harvested in March-April, so in January the wheat crop would be clearly visible in the fields as standing green crop. Paddy and Maize are Kharif crops sown in summer, and Jowar is also a Kharif crop, so none of them would be visible in January.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) गेहूँ है। जनवरी रबी फसल का मौसम है। दिल्ली से चंडीगढ़ का मार्ग हरियाणा और पंजाब से होकर जाता है, जो गेहूँ उत्पादन के प्रमुख राज्य हैं। जनवरी में गेहूँ की हरी फसल खेतों में स्पष्ट दिखेगी।

questions.text: नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं। ये अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) हैं। दोनों कथनों को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए: अभिकथन (A): खनिज हमारे जीवन के अति अनिवार्य भाग हैं। कारण (R): सभी सजीव वस्तुओं को खनिजों की आवश्यकता होती है।
questions.text_english: Two statements are given below. They are Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Read both the statements carefully and choose the correct option: Assertion (A): Minerals are an indispensable part of our lives. Reason (R): All living things need minerals.

options.A: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Minerals are indeed an indispensable part of our lives because all living organisms — plants, animals, and humans — require minerals for various biological processes such as bone formation, enzyme function, and cellular metabolism. Since all living things need minerals (R), this is the correct explanation for why minerals are an indispensable part of our lives (A).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है। सभी सजीव प्राणियों को खनिजों की आवश्यकता होती है, इसीलिए खनिज हमारे जीवन का अनिवार्य हिस्सा हैं।

questions.text: नीचे दो कथन I एवं II दिए गए हैं। दोनों कथनों को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए: कथन I: प्रौद्योगिकी में तीव्र उन्नति वैश्वीकरण की प्रक्रिया को उत्प्रेरित करने वाला एक मुख्य कारक है। कथन II: इसने लंबी दूरियों तक वस्तुओं की तीव्रतर आपूर्ति को कम लागत पर संभव किया है।
questions.text_english: Two statements I and II are given below. Read both the statements carefully and choose the correct option: Statement I: Rapid improvement in technology has been one major factor to stimulate the globalisation process. Statement II: This has made much faster delivery of goods across long distances possible at lower costs.

options.A: कथन I और II दोनों सही हैं और कथन II, कथन I की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: कथन I और II दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कथन II, कथन I की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: कथन I सही है, परन्तु कथन II गलत है।
options.D: कथन I गलत है, परन्तु कथन II सही है।

options_english.A: Both statements I and II are correct and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.
options_english.B: Both statements I and II are correct, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
options_english.C: Statement I is correct, but statement II is incorrect.
options_english.D: Statement I is incorrect, but statement II is correct.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I. Technological advancement has indeed been a major driver of globalisation. Statement II directly explains how — by enabling faster delivery of goods over long distances at lower costs through improvements in transportation, communication, and logistics technology. This reduction in cost and time has accelerated the process of globalisation by making international trade more viable and efficient.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। दोनों कथन सही हैं और कथन II, कथन I की सही व्याख्या है। प्रौद्योगिकी उन्नति ने परिवहन की लागत घटाकर और गति बढ़ाकर वैश्वीकरण को प्रोत्साहित किया है।

questions.text: भारत के शहरी क्षेत्रों में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा समूह अपनी ऋण की आवश्यकताओं को पूरा करने के लिए अनौपचारिक स्रोतों पर निर्भर है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following groups in urban India depend on informal sources to meet their credit needs?

options.C: दोनों, ग़रीब और कम संपत्ति वाले परिवार
options.D: दोनों, समृद्ध और कम संपत्ति वाले परिवार

options_english.C: Both poor households and households with few assets
options_english.D: Both well-off households and households with few assets

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Both poor households and households with few assets. In urban India, both poor households and households with few assets rely on informal sources of credit such as moneylenders, friends, relatives, and employers. This is because they lack the necessary collateral, documentation, and credit history required to access formal banking channels. Well-off households, by contrast, generally have sufficient assets and credit history to access formal credit from banks and other financial institutions.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) दोनों, ग़रीब और कम संपत्ति वाले परिवार है। शहरी भारत में ये दोनों वर्ग जमानत और दस्तावेज़ों की कमी के कारण औपचारिक बैंकों से ऋण नहीं ले पाते और अनौपचारिक स्रोतों पर निर्भर रहते हैं।
questions.topic: Formal and Informal Sources of Credit

questions.text: ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में किसानों के लिए सरकारी बैंकों से ऋण लेना कठिन क्यों हो जाता है? निम्नलिखित कारणों को पढ़िए और सबसे उपयुक्त विकल्प का चयन कीजिए: I. ऋणाधार का अभाव, II. जटिल प्रक्रिया, III. ऋण की उच्चतर लागत, IV. जागरूकता का अभाव
questions.text_english: Why does it become difficult for farmers in rural areas to take loans from government banks? Read the following reasons and choose the most appropriate option: I. Lack of collateral, II. Complicated procedure, III. Higher cost of borrowing, IV. Lack of awareness

options.A: केवल I, II और III सही हैं।
options.B: केवल II, III और IV सही हैं।
options.C: केवल I, II और IV सही हैं।
options.D: केवल I, III और IV सही हैं।

options_english.A: Only I, II and III are correct.
options_english.B: Only II, III and IV are correct.
options_english.C: Only I, II and IV are correct.
options_english.D: Only I, III and IV are correct.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Only I, II and IV are correct. Rural farmers face difficulty in accessing formal bank credit primarily because they lack collateral (I) such as land or property documents to pledge, the procedure is complicated (II) involving extensive paperwork and documentation, and they often lack awareness (IV) about loan schemes and procedures. Higher cost of borrowing (III) is actually a characteristic of informal sources like moneylenders, not formal bank loans, which charge lower interest rates. Therefore, III is incorrect in this context.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) केवल I, II और IV सही हैं। ग्रामीण किसानों को ऋणाधार का अभाव, जटिल प्रक्रिया और जागरूकता की कमी के कारण सरकारी बैंकों से ऋण लेने में कठिनाई होती है। उच्च ब्याज दर अनौपचारिक स्रोतों की विशेषता है, सरकारी बैंकों की नहीं।

questions.text: दिए गए चित्र को देखिए और उसके नीचे दिए गए प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए: चित्र में किया जाने वाला कार्य अर्थव्यवस्था के किस क्षेत्रक के अंतर्गत आता है?
questions.text_english: Look at the given picture and answer the question that follow: The work being done in the picture falls under which sector of the economy?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Secondary. The picture shows workers engaged in garment manufacturing or textile processing in a factory setting. Manufacturing and processing activities, where raw materials are transformed into finished goods, fall under the Secondary Sector of the economy. The Primary sector involves agriculture and extraction, the Tertiary sector involves services, and the Quaternary sector involves knowledge-based activities. Since the image depicts industrial manufacturing, it belongs to the Secondary Sector.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) द्वितीयक है। चित्र में कपड़ा निर्माण या परिधान उद्योग में काम दिखाया गया है। कच्चे माल को तैयार माल में बदलने की प्रक्रिया द्वितीयक क्षेत्रक के अंतर्गत आती है।

questions.text: 'X' एक कस्बे में रहता है। वह फूलों की खेती के साथ-साथ पशुपालन भी करता है। 'X' का कार्य अर्थव्यवस्था के किस क्षेत्रक के अंतर्गत आएगा?
questions.text_english: 'X' lives in a town. He cultivates flowers along with animal husbandry. The work of 'X' will fall under which sector of the economy?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Primary. The Primary Sector includes all activities that involve the direct use of natural resources, such as agriculture, fishing, mining, forestry, and animal husbandry. 'X' cultivates flowers (agriculture) and also does animal husbandry (rearing of animals). Both of these activities belong to the Primary Sector because they directly depend on nature and natural processes. The location of the person (a town or village) does not change the classification of the economic activity.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) प्राथमिक है। फूलों की खेती और पशुपालन दोनों प्राकृतिक संसाधनों पर आधारित गतिविधियाँ हैं, जो प्राथमिक क्षेत्रक के अंतर्गत आती हैं। कस्बे में रहने से गतिविधि का वर्गीकरण नहीं बदलता।

questions.text: लैंगिक असमानता को दूर करने के कोई दो उपाय सुझाइए।
questions.text_english: Suggest any two measures to remove gender inequality.

key_points: Equal educational opportunities for girls and boys.
Equal pay for equal work and ensuring women's participation in political processes.

questions.solution: Two important measures to remove gender inequality are: First, providing equal educational opportunities to girls and boys at all levels, from primary school to higher education, which empowers women economically and socially. Second, ensuring equal pay for equal work and encouraging women's active participation in politics, decision-making, and professional fields through reservations and awareness programmes.
questions.solution_hindi: लैंगिक असमानता दूर करने के दो उपाय: पहला, लड़कियों और लड़कों को शिक्षा के समान अवसर प्रदान करना ताकि महिलाएँ आर्थिक और सामाजिक रूप से सशक्त हों। दूसरा, समान कार्य के लिए समान वेतन सुनिश्चित करना और राजनीति व नीति-निर्माण में महिलाओं की सक्रिय भागीदारी बढ़ाना।

questions.text: काली मृदा की दो प्रमुख विशेषताओं की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain two important characteristics of Black soil.

key_points: Black soil has high moisture-retaining capacity and is rich in calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, and lime.
It is ideal for cotton cultivation and swells when wet while developing wide cracks when dry.

questions.solution: Black soil, also known as regur soil, has two important characteristics. First, it has an exceptionally high moisture-retaining capacity, which makes it very fertile and suitable for crops even during dry spells. It is rich in minerals like calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, and lime. Second, it is self-ploughing in nature — it swells and becomes sticky when wet, and develops wide cracks when dry, which helps in natural aeration and mixing of the soil, making it ideal for cotton cultivation.
questions.solution_hindi: काली मृदा (रेगड़ मिट्टी) की दो प्रमुख विशेषताएँ हैं: पहली, इसमें नमी धारण करने की अत्यधिक क्षमता होती है और यह कैल्शियम कार्बोनेट, मैग्नेशियम, पोटाश तथा चूने जैसे खनिजों से समृद्ध होती है। दूसरी, यह स्वतः जुताई करने वाली मिट्टी है — गीली होने पर फूलती है और सूखने पर गहरी दरारें पड़ जाती हैं, जो कपास की खेती के लिए आदर्श है।

sub_questions.text: भारत में 'आधुनिक राष्ट्रवाद' के उदय में उपनिवेशवाद विरोधी आंदोलन की भूमिका को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the role of anti-colonial movement in the rise of 'modern nationalism' in India.

key_points: Anti-colonial movements united diverse groups under a common identity against British rule.
They fostered a sense of shared history and collective nationhood, giving rise to modern nationalism.

sub_questions.solution: The anti-colonial movement played a crucial role in the rise of modern nationalism in India. As people from different regions, castes, and religions came together to oppose British rule, they developed a shared sense of identity and belonging to one nation. The struggle against colonial exploitation created a common political consciousness. Leaders like Gandhi mobilised masses across social boundaries, transforming personal grievances into a collective national identity and aspiration for independence.

sub_questions.text: गाँधीजी ने क्यों कहा कि 'सत्याग्रह तो शुद्ध आत्मबल है'? दो तर्क देकर स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Why did Gandhiji say 'Satyagraha is pure soul-force'? Explain by giving two arguments.

key_points: Satyagraha relies on truth and moral strength, not physical violence.
It appeals to the conscience of the oppressor and seeks to convert rather than coerce.

sub_questions.solution: Gandhiji called Satyagraha 'pure soul-force' for two key reasons. First, it is based entirely on truth and moral courage rather than physical force or weapons — a Satyagrahi wins by the power of his conscience and righteousness, not by harming others. Second, it aims to convert the oppressor by appealing to his conscience and humanity, rather than defeating him through coercion. This makes it a spiritually superior form of resistance that transforms both the practitioner and the opponent.

questions.solution: This question has two internal options (a) and (b). Answers are provided in sub_questions.

questions.text: परिवहन प्रौद्योगिकी में हुई उन्नति ने किस प्रकार वैश्वीकरण प्रक्रिया को उत्प्रेरित किया? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: How did improvement in transportation technology stimulate the globalisation process? Explain.

key_points: Faster and cheaper transportation reduced the cost of moving goods across long distances.
Improvements like container shipping and air cargo enabled rapid international trade, stimulating globalisation.

questions.solution: Improvements in transportation technology have greatly stimulated the globalisation process in two important ways. First, the development of container ships, faster railways, and air cargo drastically reduced the time and cost of transporting goods across continents, making international trade economically viable. Second, cheaper and faster transportation enabled multinational companies to source raw materials, manufacture, and sell products across different countries efficiently, creating global supply chains and deepening economic interdependence among nations.
questions.solution_hindi: परिवहन प्रौद्योगिकी में सुधार ने वैश्वीकरण को दो प्रकार से उत्प्रेरित किया: पहला, कंटेनर जहाज और हवाई माल परिवहन के विकास से माल की ढुलाई सस्ती और तेज हुई। दूसरा, बहुराष्ट्रीय कंपनियाँ विभिन्न देशों से कच्चा माल मँगाकर और तैयार माल भेजकर वैश्विक आपूर्ति श्रृंखला बना सकीं।

questions.text: ''राष्ट्रवाद का विचार भारतीय लोक कथाओं को पुनर्जीवित करने के आंदोलन से मज़बूत हुआ।'' राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन के संदर्भ में इस कथन की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: "The ideas of nationalism developed through a movement to revive Indian folklore." Explain the statement in the context of the national movement.

key_points: Indian nationalists revived folk songs, legends, and oral traditions to create a shared cultural identity.
Artists and writers used folk traditions to inspire pride in India's heritage and resist colonial cultural dominance.
Rabindranath Tagore and others led this cultural revival, linking local traditions to the idea of a unified nation.

questions.solution: During the national movement, Indian nationalists realised that nationalism could be strengthened by reviving India's rich folk traditions. Leaders like Rabindranath Tagore actively promoted the collection and celebration of folk songs, local legends, and oral traditions to awaken a sense of shared cultural heritage among diverse communities. Artists depicted scenes from Indian mythology and history to instil pride and create a unified national identity. By connecting people to their common past and indigenous culture, this movement countered British claims of cultural superiority and helped transform regional identities into a broader sense of belonging to one Indian nation, thus strengthening nationalist consciousness across the country.
questions.solution_hindi: राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन के दौरान राष्ट्रवादियों ने भारतीय लोककथाओं को पुनर्जीवित करने पर बल दिया। रवींद्रनाथ टैगोर जैसे विद्वानों ने लोकगीतों, किंवदंतियों और मौखिक परंपराओं को एकत्रित कर एक साझा सांस्कृतिक पहचान बनाई। इससे ब्रिटिश सांस्कृतिक वर्चस्व का प्रतिरोध हुआ और विविध समुदायों में 'हम एक राष्ट्र हैं' की भावना जागृत हुई।

questions.text:
रिंझा की कहानी को पढ़िए और उसके नीचे दिए गए प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए:

रिंझा की कहानी

रिंझा असम में डिफु के बाहरी क्षेत्र में अपने परिवार के साथ एक छोटे गाँव में रहती है। वह अपने परिवार के सदस्यों द्वारा एक भूमि के टुकड़े पर उगी वनस्पति को काटकर व जलाकर साफ करते देख कर आनंद का अनुभव करती है। वह प्राय: परिवार के सदस्यों के साथ बाँस के नाले द्वारा समीप के झरने से पानी लाकर अपने खेत को सिंचित करने में सहायता करती है। वह अपने परिस्थान से लगाव रखती है और जब तक संभव हो यहाँ रहना चाहती है। परन्तु इस छोटी बच्ची को अपने खेत में मिट्टी की घटती उर्वरता के बारे में कुछ भी पता नहीं है जिसके कारण उसके परिवार को अगले वर्ष नए भूमि के टुकड़े की तलाश करनी होगी।

रिंझा का परिवार किस प्रकार की खेती कर रहा है? उसकी किन्हीं दो विशेषताओं का वर्णन कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
Read the story of Rinjha and answer the question that follows:

Story of Rinjha

Rinjha lived with her family in a small village at the outskirts of Diphu in Assam. She enjoys watching her family members clearing, slashing and burning a patch of land for cultivation. She often helps them in irrigating the fields with water running through a bamboo canal from the nearby spring. She loves the surroundings and wants to stay here as long as she can, but this little girl has no idea about the declining fertility of the soil and her family's search for a fresh patch of land in the next season.

What type of farming is Rinjha's family doing? Describe any two of its characteristics.

key_points: Rinjha's family practises Shifting Cultivation (also called Slash and Burn or Jhum cultivation).
Land is cleared by cutting and burning vegetation; after soil fertility declines, farmers move to a new patch.
It uses primitive tools and depends on natural water sources; no chemical fertilisers are used.

questions.solution: Rinjha's family is practising Shifting Cultivation, also known as Slash and Burn agriculture or Jhum cultivation. It is called so because the family clears a patch of forest by cutting and burning vegetation, cultivates it for a few years until the soil loses its fertility, and then moves to a new patch. Two characteristics are: First, it involves clearing land by slash and burn method — vegetation is cut down and burned to add nutrients to the soil temporarily. Second, once the soil fertility declines, the family abandons the plot and moves to a new patch of land every season, making it a nomadic form of farming with no permanent settlement or ownership.
questions.solution_hindi: रिंझा का परिवार स्थानांतरण कृषि (झूम खेती) कर रहा है। इसकी दो विशेषताएँ हैं: पहली, खेती के लिए वनस्पति को काटकर जलाया जाता है जिससे मिट्टी में अस्थायी पोषक तत्व मिल जाते हैं। दूसरी, मिट्टी की उर्वरता घटने पर परिवार नए भूखंड की तलाश करता है और पुराना स्थान छोड़ देता है।

questions.text: "राजनीतिक सत्ता का बँटवारा नहीं किया जा सकता।" इस कथन के विरुद्ध उपयुक्त तर्कों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
questions.text_english: "Political power cannot be divided." Analyse suitable arguments against the statement.

key_points: Power sharing prevents concentration of power and avoids tyranny.
It accommodates diversity and ensures representation of all groups.
Federal examples like India and Belgium show successful power-sharing models.

questions.solution: The statement that political power cannot be divided is incorrect, and there are strong arguments against it. First, power-sharing is essential in diverse societies to prevent the concentration of authority in one hand, which can lead to tyranny or majoritarianism. Second, in a democracy, sharing power among different organs such as the legislature, executive, and judiciary ensures checks and balances, protecting citizens' rights. Third, countries like India and Belgium have successfully divided power through federal systems, giving different levels of government their own domains, proving that power-sharing is not only possible but also beneficial for political stability and social harmony.

Second, parties that win elections form the government, frame policies, and pass laws, while losing parties form the opposition and hold the government accountable. It encompasses a wide range of activities including banking, finance, insurance, trade, transport, communication, IT services, education, and healthcare. Over the past three decades, the service sector has grown rapidly, particularly in IT and business process outsourcing, making India a global hub for services. However, despite its large GDP share, the sector does not employ a proportionally large percentage of the workforce, indicating a structural imbalance. Nevertheless, its contribution to economic growth, foreign exchange earnings, and employment in urban areas is indispensable.

sub_questions.text_english: "Culture played an important role in creating the idea of the nation in 19th century Europe." Evaluate the statement in the context of romanticism.

key_points: Romanticism was a cultural movement that emphasised emotion, nature, and folk traditions over reason.
Romantic artists, poets, and musicians created a shared cultural identity by celebrating national history, language, and folklore.
Johann Gottfried Herder argued that true German spirit lived in folk songs and dialects.
Romantic composers like Karol Kurpinski used folk music to stir nationalist feelings.
This cultural nationalism preceded and inspired political nationalism across Europe.

sub_questions.solution: The statement is entirely valid. In 19th century Europe, Romanticism played a pivotal role in shaping national consciousness. Romanticism was a cultural movement that reacted against the emphasis on reason and instead celebrated emotion, nature, local traditions, and folk heritage. Romantic thinkers like Johann Gottfried Herder argued that the true essence of a nation lay in its folk culture — songs, stories, and dialects — rather than in political institutions. Romantic poets and writers like Wordsworth and Goethe glorified national landscapes, mythologies, and history to awaken emotional attachment to the homeland. In Poland, the composer Karol Kurpinski used folk music and dance forms to keep national consciousness alive during foreign occupation. Similarly, French Romantic painter Eugene Delacroix used dramatic imagery of historical events to stir nationalist sentiment. Vernacular languages were promoted as symbols of national identity, making culture a powerful tool in creating the idea of a shared nation before formal political nationalism could take root.

sub_questions.text: "1871 के बाद यूरोप में गंभीर राष्ट्रवादी तनाव का स्रोत बाल्कन क्षेत्र था।" स्लाव आंदोलन के संदर्भ में इस कथन का मूल्यांकन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: "The most serious source of nationalist tension in Europe after 1871 was the area called the Balkans." Evaluate the statement in context of Slavic Movement.

key_points: The Balkans comprised modern-day Romania, Bulgaria, Albania, Greece, Croatia, Bosnia, Serbia, Slovenia, Macedonia.
The Ottoman Empire was disintegrating, creating a power vacuum that intensified nationalist tensions.
The Slavic peoples of the region sought independence and unity, supported by Russia.
Austria-Hungary and the Ottoman Empire opposed Slavic nationalism, leading to conflicts.
This competition among European powers over the Balkans became a major cause of World War I.

sub_questions.solution: The statement is accurate and well-supported by historical evidence. After 1871, the Balkans — encompassing modern territories of Romania, Bulgaria, Albania, Greece, Bosnia, Serbia, and others — became the most explosive centre of nationalist tension in Europe. The region was inhabited by diverse Slavic peoples who had been dominated by the declining Ottoman Empire. As the Ottoman Empire weakened, these Slavic groups, inspired by Romantic nationalism, sought self-determination and unity. The Slavic movement, supported by Russia which considered itself the protector of Slavic peoples, demanded freedom from both Ottoman and Austro-Hungarian control. Austria-Hungary and the Ottoman Empire strongly opposed Slavic nationalism as it threatened their territorial integrity. This created rival alliances, with Russia backing Slavic groups and Austria-Hungary opposing them. The intense competition among European imperial powers — Germany, Austria-Hungary, Russia, Britain, France — for control over the weakening Ottoman territories made the Balkans a perpetual flashpoint. The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo in 1914 by a Slavic nationalist ultimately triggered World War I, confirming that Balkan nationalism was indeed the most serious source of European tension after 1871.

sub_questions.text_english: "Recent evidence suggests that overuse of groundwater is becoming a serious threat in many parts of the country." Evaluate the statement in the context of sustainability of development.

key_points: Overuse of groundwater depletes a non-renewable natural resource, threatening future generations.
Declining water tables affect agriculture, drinking water supply, and ecosystems.
Sustainable development requires using resources at a rate that allows natural replenishment.
Measures like rainwater harvesting and efficient irrigation are needed.
Short-term economic growth through overexploitation conflicts with long-term sustainable development goals.

sub_questions.solution: The statement is a serious warning about the unsustainable use of groundwater, which directly conflicts with the principle of sustainable development. Sustainable development means meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. Groundwater is a finite natural resource that replenishes slowly. In states like Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan, intensive agriculture using tube wells has caused water tables to fall alarmingly. This threatens agricultural productivity, drinking water availability, and natural ecosystems. Overuse of groundwater is essentially borrowing from future generations and reducing their resource base. Sustainable development demands that we adopt water conservation measures such as rainwater harvesting, drip irrigation, and watershed management to ensure groundwater levels are maintained. Without addressing this crisis, short-term economic gains will come at the cost of irreversible long-term environmental damage, directly undermining the goals of sustainable and equitable development for future generations.

sub_questions.text: "विभिन्न श्रेणी के लोगों के विकास के लक्ष्य भिन्न हो सकते हैं।" इस कथन का मूल्यांकन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: "The development goals of different categories of people may differ." Evaluate the statement.

key_points: Development is not a single uniform concept — different people have different needs and aspirations.
A landless labourer desires more income and job security; a landlord may want better crop prices.
Aspirations differ by gender, class, region, and occupation.
What benefits one group may harm another — a dam may benefit farmers but displace tribal communities.
Development must consider diverse and sometimes conflicting goals to be truly inclusive.

sub_questions.solution: The statement is absolutely correct. Development cannot be viewed as a single, uniform process because different people have fundamentally different needs, aspirations, and life circumstances. For example, a landless agricultural labourer desires more days of employment, higher wages, and better wages, while a farmer who owns land may want higher prices for crops or better irrigation facilities. A woman working in an urban factory may prioritise safety and fair wages, while a student aspires for quality education and employment opportunities. What constitutes development for one group may actually harm another — construction of a large dam may provide irrigation and electricity to farmers in the plains but displace thousands of tribal families from their ancestral lands. Therefore, any genuine evaluation of development must account for these diverse and sometimes conflicting goals, ensuring that progress for one section of society does not come at the expense of another, making development truly inclusive and just.

sub_questions.text: "लोकतंत्र की एक खासियत है कि इसकी जाँच-परख कभी खत्म नहीं होती।" उपयुक्त तर्कों सहित कथन की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: "One distinct feature of democracy is that its scrutiny never ends." Explain the statement with appropriate arguments.

key_points: Democracy is a system of continuous self-evaluation and reform.
Citizens have the right and responsibility to evaluate government performance through elections, media, and protests.
No democracy is perfect — it is always a work in progress.
Free press and civil society ensure that governments remain accountable at all times.
Democratic institutions evolve through ongoing scrutiny, making democracy stronger over time.

sub_questions.solution: The statement captures one of the most important features of democracy — its capacity for continuous self-examination and improvement. Unlike authoritarian regimes, democracy does not claim to be a finished or perfect system. It is always a work in progress. First, citizens in a democracy have the right to question, criticise, and evaluate their government through elections, public protests, free media, and civil society organisations. Second, democratic institutions like the judiciary, parliament, and press serve as constant watchdogs, scrutinising the exercise of power by the executive. Third, the periodic elections ensure that leaders remain accountable and can be removed if they fail to perform. Fourth, democracies around the world have faced and continue to face challenges such as corruption, inequality, and communal tensions, and they address these challenges through public debate and institutional reform. This ongoing scrutiny makes democracy a living, evolving system rather than a static one, continuously striving to better fulfil the aspirations of its people.

sub_questions.text: "लोकतांत्रिक व्यवस्था अन्य व्यवस्थाओं से बेहतर है।" उपयुक्त तर्कों सहित कथन की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: "Democratic system is better than other systems." Explain the statement with appropriate arguments.

key_points: Democracy ensures equality — every citizen has one vote regardless of wealth or status.
It protects individual rights and liberties through constitutions and law.
Accountability through regular elections prevents abuse of power.
Democracy promotes dignity and respects diversity by giving voice to all groups.
It resolves conflicts peacefully through dialogue, unlike authoritarian systems.

sub_questions.solution: Democracy is widely considered superior to other systems of government for several compelling reasons. First, democracy upholds the principle of equality — every adult citizen has an equal vote regardless of their wealth, caste, gender, or religion, ensuring that political power is not monopolised by a privileged few. Second, democratic governments are accountable to the people through regular elections, which allows citizens to remove ineffective or corrupt leaders peacefully, a mechanism absent in authoritarian systems. Third, democracy protects fundamental rights and civil liberties through a constitution and an independent judiciary, safeguarding individuals from state tyranny. Fourth, democracies are better equipped to handle social diversity and conflicts peacefully through dialogue, negotiation, and compromise rather than suppression. Fifth, democracy promotes political participation, which gives citizens a sense of dignity and ownership over their governance. While democracies are imperfect and face many challenges, their ability to self-correct through scrutiny makes them more responsive and just than monarchies, dictatorships, or one-party systems.

sub_questions.text_english: "Manufacturing industries are considered the backbone of the economic development of a country." Justify the statement.

key_points: Manufacturing transforms raw materials into value-added finished goods, increasing national income.
It generates large-scale employment in both urban and rural areas.
It reduces dependence on agriculture and diversifies the economy.
It earns foreign exchange through exports of manufactured goods.
Industrial development stimulates growth in other sectors — transport, services, trade.

sub_questions.solution: Manufacturing industries are rightly called the backbone of economic development for several important reasons. First, they transform raw materials into finished, value-added goods, thereby increasing national income and GDP significantly. Second, the manufacturing sector generates massive employment opportunities — directly in factories and indirectly in supporting industries, transport, and services — reducing poverty and unemployment. Third, industrialisation reduces a country's dependence on agriculture and creates a diversified, resilient economy that can withstand fluctuations in agricultural output. Fourth, manufactured goods are major items of export, earning vital foreign exchange that can be used to import technology and capital goods. Fifth, industrial development creates a multiplier effect — growth in manufacturing stimulates expansion in transport, banking, trade, and service sectors. Countries like China and South Korea demonstrate how rapid industrialisation can transform economies from developing to developed within a few decades, confirming that manufacturing is indeed the engine of economic development.

sub_questions.text: "कृषि तथा उद्योग एक-दूसरे के पूरक हैं।" इस कथन को न्यायसंगत ठहराइए।
sub_questions.text_english: "Agriculture and industries complement each other." Justify the statement.

key_points: Agriculture supplies raw materials to agro-based industries like sugar, cotton textiles, and jute.
Industries manufacture agricultural inputs like fertilisers, pesticides, and machinery.
Industrial growth creates demand for agricultural products as food for urban workers.
Agricultural prosperity increases purchasing power, boosting demand for industrial goods.
Both sectors together drive India's overall economic growth and employment.

sub_questions.solution: Agriculture and industries are deeply complementary and mutually dependent sectors of the economy. Agriculture supplies essential raw materials to a wide range of agro-based industries — cotton to textile mills, sugarcane to sugar factories, jute to jute mills, and oilseeds to vegetable oil plants. Without agricultural output, these industries would have no raw material base. Conversely, industries supply agriculture with critical inputs — fertilisers, pesticides, high-yielding seed technology, tractors, pump sets, and irrigation equipment — that have dramatically increased agricultural productivity during the Green Revolution and beyond. Growing industrial towns create a large urban workforce that needs food, thus generating demand for agricultural produce. In turn, agricultural prosperity raises farmers' incomes, increasing their purchasing power and creating demand for industrial goods like vehicles, consumer electronics, and construction materials. This symbiotic relationship between the two sectors ensures that the growth of one promotes the growth of the other, making them true complements in driving India's economic development.

An Experiment in Brazil

A city called Porto Alegre in Brazil has carried out an extraordinary experiment in combining decentralisation with participative democracy. The city has set up a parallel organisation operating alongside the municipal council, enabling local inhabitants to take real decisions for their city. Just as Porto Alegre divides the city into wards with local meetings for direct citizen participation, India has Gram Sabhas at the village level where all adult voters of the village can participate in discussions and decision-making about local development, budget allocation, and governance. The elected Gram Panchayat implements decisions, but the Gram Sabha provides the platform for grassroots participatory democracy, ensuring local self-governance.

Loans From Cooperatives

Besides banks, the other major source of cheap credit in rural areas are the cooperative societies (or cooperatives). Members of a cooperative pool their resources for cooperation in certain areas. There are several types of cooperatives possible such as farmers cooperatives, weavers cooperatives, industrial workers cooperatives, etc. Krishak Cooperative functions in a village not very far away from Sonpur. It has 2300 farmers as members. It accepts deposits from its members. With these deposits as collateral, the Cooperative has obtained a large loan from the bank. These funds are used to provide loans to members. Once these loans are repaid, another round of lending can take place. Krishak Cooperative provides loans for the purchase of agricultural implements, loans for cultivation and agricultural trade, fishery loans, loans for construction of houses and for a variety of other expenses.

sub_questions.text: सहकारी समितियाँ ऋण के किस स्रोत के अंतर्गत आती हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: Cooperative societies come under which source of credit?

key_points: Cooperative societies come under the formal (institutional) source of credit.

sub_questions.solution: Cooperative societies come under the formal (or institutional) source of credit. They are registered organisations regulated by the government and provide credit at lower interest rates compared to informal sources like moneylenders. They are an important part of the formal financial system, especially in rural areas where commercial banks may have limited reach.

sub_questions.text: सहकारी समितियों की पूँजी के किन्हीं दो स्रोतों का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Mention any two sources of capital of cooperative societies.

key_points: Deposits from members.
Loans obtained from banks using member deposits as collateral.

sub_questions.solution: Two sources of capital for cooperative societies are: first, deposits collected from their own members, who pool their savings into the cooperative as a form of collective resource-building; second, loans obtained from commercial banks, where the cooperative uses its member deposits as collateral to secure large institutional loans, which are then distributed to members at subsidised rates.

sub_questions.text: किसानों की आय वृद्धि में सहकारी समितियों की भूमिका को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the role of cooperative societies in increasing the income of farmers.

key_points: Cooperatives provide cheap credit, reducing dependence on moneylenders and saving farmers from debt traps.
They finance purchase of agricultural inputs and equipment, improving productivity and farm income.

sub_questions.solution: Cooperative societies play a vital role in increasing farmers' incomes in several ways. First, they provide loans at low interest rates for purchasing seeds, fertilisers, pesticides, and agricultural equipment, which improves farm productivity and output without the burden of high-interest informal debt. Second, by offering credit for cultivation, trade, house construction, and other needs, cooperatives free farmers from exploitative moneylenders who charge exorbitant interest rates that trap farmers in cycles of poverty. Lower borrowing costs mean farmers retain more of their earnings, directly increasing their net income and improving their standard of living.

Print and Censorship

The power of the printed word is most often seen in the way governments seek to regulate and suppress print. The colonial government kept continuous track of all books and newspapers published in India and passed numerous laws to control the press. During the First World War, under the Defence of India Rules, 22 newspapers had to furnish securities. Of these, 18 shut down rather than comply with government orders. The Sedition Committee Report under Rowlatt in 1919 further strengthened controls that led to imposition of penalties on various newspapers. At the outbreak of the Second World War, the Defence of India Act was passed, allowing censoring of reports of war-related topics. All reports about the Quit India movement came under its purview. In August 1942, about 90 newspapers were suppressed.

sub_questions.text: 'सेंसर' का अर्थ स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the meaning of 'censor'.

key_points: Censorship means the official suppression or restriction of published material — books, newspapers, films — that the government considers politically dangerous or objectionable.

sub_questions.solution: Censorship means the official examination and suppression of published or broadcast material by a government authority. It involves restricting or banning information, news reports, books, or films that the government considers politically dangerous, seditious, or harmful to public order. In the passage, the colonial government censored Indian newspapers to prevent reporting on the Quit India movement and anti-British nationalist activities.

sub_questions.text: औपनिवेशिक प्रशासन किताबों और पत्र-पत्रिकाओं पर क्यों नज़र रखता था?
sub_questions.text_english: Why did the colonial administration keep an eye on books and newspapers?

key_points: The colonial administration monitored print media because nationalist ideas spread through books and newspapers threatened British rule and could mobilise public opinion against the government.

sub_questions.solution: The colonial administration kept a close watch on books and newspapers because it feared the power of the printed word to spread nationalist ideas, anti-British sentiment, and calls for independence. Newspapers and books could mobilise large sections of the Indian public against British rule, organise resistance movements, and expose colonial exploitation. To suppress dissent and maintain control, the government passed laws to censor and regulate the press, ensuring that critical voices could not freely communicate with the masses.

sub_questions.text: गाँधीजी ने रॉलट एक्ट के विरुद्ध देशव्यापी सत्याग्रह क्यों शुरू किया? किन्हीं दो कारणों को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Why did Gandhiji start a nationwide Satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act? Explain any two reasons.

key_points: The Rowlatt Act (1919) allowed the British to imprison any Indian without trial, violating civil liberties.
It was seen as a deeply unjust and repressive law that denied Indians basic rights, making mass resistance necessary.

sub_questions.solution: Gandhiji launched a nationwide Satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act of 1919 for two important reasons. First, the Rowlatt Act gave the British government sweeping powers to arrest and imprison any Indian suspected of sedition without a trial and without the possibility of appeal — a clear violation of civil liberties and natural justice that Gandhiji found morally intolerable. Second, the Act was passed despite unanimous opposition from all elected Indian members of the Imperial Legislative Council, exposing the colonial government's total disregard for Indian opinion and democratic principles. Gandhiji believed that such an unjust and repressive law must be resisted through peaceful but determined mass civil disobedience across the entire country.
